{"command": "create", "path": "/memories/repo/core-exotic-subdep-fix.md", "file_text": "# Fixed ERR_PNPM_EXOTIC_SUBDEP for create-pantoken-app (2026-09-08)

## Root cause
`@pantoken/core`'s package.json declared `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` (a
`github:`-protocol, i.e. "exotic", pnpm catalog entry) as a real `dependencies` entry — needed only
by `buildTokens()` in `src/build.ts` (the internal, upstream-resolving transform used solely by
`formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` at monorepo build time). But `platforms/{android,compose,
flutter,rust,swift}` all depend on `@pantoken/core` as a runtime `dependencies` entry too (for
`toStyleDictionary`/icon-asset helpers, which never touch the upstream package). Since core bundled
to a SINGLE `dist/index.mjs` (tsdown one-entry), any consumer importing anything from `@pantoken/core`
transitively required `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` to be installed — an end user
installing `@pantoken/pantoken` (which depends on all those platform packages) hit
`ERR_PNPM_EXOTIC_SUBDEP` because the git-hosted package showed up as a subdependency (2+ levels deep),
which pnpm's `blockExoticSubdeps` policy (apparently on by default for at least some pnpm versions/
configs, even though this repo's own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` doesn't set it) rejects.

## Fix (packages/core)
1. `vite.config.ts`: switched from `pack: { exports: true }` (single bundle) to
   `pack: { entry: { index: "src/index.ts", build: "src/build.ts" }, exports: false }` — same pattern
   as `plugin-kit`'s sandbox split (see `utils-package-node-only-modules.md`).
2. `package.json`: added `"./build": "./dist/build.mjs"` to `exports`; moved
   `"@instructure/instructure-design-tokens"` from `dependencies` to `devDependencies` (still resolves
   fine for in-repo builds — pnpm installs devDependencies for workspace member packages the same as
   deps; only PUBLISHED consumers stop seeing it).
3. `src/index.ts`: removed `export { buildTokens }` (moved to the new `build.ts` entry only).
4. `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` (the only real runtime consumer of `buildTokens`): import from
   `@pantoken/core/build` instead of `@pantoken/core`. Updated its `generate.test.ts` mock target to
   match.
5. Updated doc-comment `@example` blocks + READMEs that showed `import { buildTokens } from
   "@pantoken/core"` to use `@pantoken/core/build` (packages/core, plugins/pantoken/{deprecations,
   simple-icons,stacking,transition,custom-icons}, formats/dtcg).

Verified: `grep instructure-design-tokens packages/core/dist/*.mjs` only matches `build.mjs`, not
`index.mjs`; rebuilt `platforms/{android,compose,flutter,rust,swift}` + `formats/icon-font` and
confirmed none of their dist bundles reference the exotic package either.

`@instructure/ui-icons` (used by `icons.ts`/`collectIcons`) is NOT exotic — it's a normal semver
registry range in the catalog, just resolved lazily via `require.resolve` at runtime, not a static
import — so it was left alone in the main entry.

## Gotchas hit while investigating
- Running `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` directly regenerates
  `formats/tokens/known-syntax-issues.json` with unrelated upstream-drift removals (design-tokens
  content has changed since the file was last committed) — `git checkout --` it after any manual
  `generate` run that isn't meant to update that file.
- `vp check`/`vp run --filter <pkg> check` in this sandboxed environment falsely reports
  `tsdoc-undefined-tag: "@module"` on EVERY file with a `@module` doc tag, even files never touched
  and even though root `tsdoc.json` defines that tag — reproduced identically on unmodified `main`.
  Pre-existing/environment-specific, not caused by package edits; don't chase it as a regression.
- Found unrelated uncommitted WIP already sitting on the `exotic-subdeps` branch before this session
  started (packages/cli/package.json + src/index.ts: lazily `import()`s `@pantoken/icon-font` as an
  optional peer dep to avoid forcing `ttf2woff2`/node-gyp native builds on all cli consumers) — that's
  a different problem (native build tooling weight), not the exotic-subdep bug; left untouched.
